**Allowed origins**

CORS is configured in `worker/src/index.ts:19-35`, in the `cors({ origin: (origin) => … })` callback passed to `app.use('*', …)`. A request origin is echoed back if it meets one of these conditions:
- It is exactly `http://localhost:4200`.
- It ends with `.pages.dev`.
- It ends with `.workers.dev`.

Any other origin gets `null`, so no CORS headers are sent. Requests with no `Origin` header also get `null`.

The rest of the CORS config:
- Methods: GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE, OPTIONS.
- Headers: `Content-Type`, `Authorization`.
- `maxAge`: 86400.

**Adding a custom domain**

Add a new condition to the `if` at `worker/src/index.ts:23-27`. For example:

```ts
origin === 'https://play.example.com' ||
```

Use an exact `===` match for a single domain. For a wildcard, use `origin.endsWith('.example.com')`. That form would also match lookalikes such as `evil-example.com`. To avoid that, include the leading dot, as in `.example.com`, or check the origin's hostname instead.

Don't put the domain in an array, because the comment at line 20 says Hono treats array entries as exact strings. The `origin` function is the only place this is enforced. I only searched `worker/` for CORS and origin handling. I didn't check `wrangler.toml` or the frontend config for anything related.
